reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing the decision and canonical bytes, returned to Articles 9–12 and 22 of the official 2026–2027 regulations, re-totalled the required and open credit across three years, and checked Appendix 5’s legal-source and argumentation outcomes. Reconsidered the offered UCR courses in the workbook and the comparison’s two organising choices against those findings. This is a separate pass by the same AI.
findings: For 2026–2027 entrants, Article 10 gives Year 1 as 27 + 27 + 6 EC including professional skills. Year 2 is 27 + 27 + 6 EC including professional skills. Semester 5 is 27 EC of courses plus 3 EC of thesis methods. Semester 6 is 3 EC professional skills, 12 EC of open choices and 15 EC of thesis. The 27 unique components total 180 EC. There is no required named track. Article 11 permits a legal internship, courses at other faculties, law courses, an approved individual project up to 6 EC or MaRBLe. MaRBLe can use the 12 EC space, with 6 EC extracurricular. The research proposal and thesis form one 18 EC component under Article 12. The proposed 2027–2028 public schedule has different components and credit allocations.

Article 22 requires two of introductory administrative, constitutional and international/European law for Semester 3, introductory private law for Semester 4, and introductory foundations, criminal law and procedure, private law and administrative law for Semester 5. Article 12 requires a passed research proposal before thesis writing. The standard 60 EC first-year plan covers the 40 EC negative-advice threshold in Articles 36–37. All required components must pass for the bachelor exam under Article 13. Appendix 5 progresses from simple legal cases to complex multidisciplinary problems and from basic source-finding to selecting and evaluating legislation, case law and literature.

The paired law courses have substantive content overlap while Dutch procedural, specialised and research training remains visible as a gap. The corrected European law pairing explains real overlap in EU institutions, competences and rules. Sociology, methods and the selected social problems sustain a genuinely different law-and-society option. The three previously invalid placements now use planned terms. The intended notes distinguish the required Maastricht thesis from optional UCR research.
